questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: What is the HCF of 84 and 126?
questions.explanation: 84 = 2 × 42 and 126 = 3 × 42; 2 and 3 are coprime.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: What is the LCM of 18 and 24?
questions.explanation: Use the highest prime powers: 2³ × 3² = 72.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A quantity increases from 240 to 300. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: Increase 60 divided by original 240 gives 25%.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sum is divided in the ratio 3:5. If the larger share is ₹250, what is the total?
questions.explanation: One part is 50; eight parts total 400.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics

questions.explanation: Total 90 minus 10 is 80; divide by four.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics

questions.explanation: Profit 120 divided by cost 800 gives 15%.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: At 10% compounded annually, ₹1,000 becomes what after two years?

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A train covers 180 km in 2.5 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time = 180 / 2.5.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics

questions.explanation: Multiply by 5/18.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A can finish work in 12 days and B in 6 days. Together they need how long?

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics

questions.explanation: Subtract 7 and divide by 3.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Find a circle's circumference for radius 7 cm, using π = 22/7.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A cube has side 4 cm. Find its volume.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: In a right triangle, sides opposite and adjacent to angle θ are 3 and 4. Find tan θ.
questions.explanation: Tangent is opposite divided by adjacent.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of an even number?
questions.explanation: Three of six outcomes are even.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Find the median of 3, 5, 8, 10, 14.
questions.explanation: The middle of five ordered observations is the third value.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: One newton accelerates one kilogram by one metre per second squared.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A body has mass 5 kg. With g = 10 m/s², its weight is what?
questions.explanation: Weight = mass × gravitational acceleration.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 200 g object occupies 50 cm³. Find density.
questions.explanation: Density = mass / volume.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A force of 10 N moves an object 5 m in the force direction. Find work.
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance along force.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A machine does 600 J of work in 3 seconds. Find power.
questions.explanation: Power = work / time.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Find kinetic energy of a 2 kg body travelling at 3 m/s.
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy = one half × mass × speed squared.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 V source is connected across a 6 Ω resistor. Find current.
questions.explanation: Ohm's law: I = V/R.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal lever has effort arm 60 cm and load arm 20 cm. Find mechanical advantage.
questions.explanation: For an ideal lever, mechanical advantage is effort arm / load arm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An 18 L mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3:2. How much water should be added to make the two quantities equal?
questions.explanation: Each of the five parts is 3.6 L. Milk exceeds water by one part, so add 3.6 L of water.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two positive integers have HCF 12 and LCM 1,260. One integer is 84. What is the other?
questions.explanation: The product of the two integers is 12 × 1,260. Dividing by 84 gives 180.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A trader bought an item for ₹640 and sold it for ₹720 after successive discounts of 10% and 20% off its marked price. What was the marked price?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 0.9 × 0.8 = 0.72 of the marked price. Thus the price before the discounts was 720/0.72.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 24 parcels is 50 kg. Four parcels with a mean mass of 65 kg are removed. What is the mean mass of the remaining parcels?
questions.explanation: The remaining mass is 24×50−4×65 = 940 kg for 20 parcels.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A needs 15 days to complete a job and B needs 20 days. They work together for 6 days. A then leaves. How many more days does B need?
questions.explanation: They complete 6(1/15+1/20) = 7/10 of the work. B completes the remaining 3/10 in 6 days.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A vehicle travels from P to Q at 48 km/h and returns by the same route at 72 km/h. Find its average speed for the complete trip.
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average is 2/(1/48+1/72) = 57.6 km/h.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 150 m train clears a 350 m bridge in 20 s. It then overtakes a cyclist moving at 5 m/s in the same direction. How many seconds does the train take to pass the cyclist?
questions.explanation: The train speed is (150+350)/20 = 25 m/s. Relative to the cyclist it gains 20 m/s, so passing takes 150/20 = 7.5 s.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A counter sells 70 tickets. Adult tickets cost ₹50 and child tickets cost ₹30. The total is ₹2,980. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: If all tickets were child tickets, the total would be ₹2,100. Each adult ticket adds ₹20. The ₹880 difference represents 44 adult tickets.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The fourth and tenth terms of an arithmetic progression are 23 and 53. What is the sum of the first 15 terms?
questions.explanation: The common difference is (53−23)/6 = 5. The first and fifteenth terms are 8 and 78, so their sum over 15 terms is 15(8+78)/2.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: What is the remainder when 7 to the power 103 is divided by 5?
questions.explanation: Seven is congruent to 2 modulo 5. The remainders of powers of 2 cycle through 2, 4, 3, 1. Exponent 103 is 3 modulo 4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A box has 5 red, 4 blue and 3 green tokens. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that exactly one is red?
questions.explanation: Select one red and one of the seven nonred tokens in 35 ways. All unordered pairs number 12×11/2 = 66.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 32 m by 24 m rectangular courtyard is surrounded by a 2 m wide path outside its boundary. The outer boundary is rectangular. What is the area of the path?
questions.explanation: The outer dimensions are 36 m by 28 m. Subtract the courtyard area from 1,008 m² to get 240 m².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 m vertical pole casts a 16 m shadow on level ground. What is the sine of the angle of elevation from the shadow tip to the pole top?
questions.explanation: The right triangle has sides 12, 16 and 20. The sine is opposite over hypotenuse, or 12/20.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A solid cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 20 cm is melted into identical spheres of radius 3 cm without loss. How many spheres can be made?
questions.explanation: The cylinder volume is 720π cm³. Each sphere has volume 36π cm³, so the count is 20.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The five observations 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14 have their smallest value replaced by 20. What are the new mean and median respectively?
questions.explanation: The new sum is 50−6+20 = 64. The sorted values are 8, 10, 12, 14 and 20, so the middle value is 12.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two pieces of different materials each have mass 300 g. Their densities are 2 and 5 g/cm³. If combined without voids or volume change, what is their overall density?
questions.explanation: Volume is 300/2 + 300/5 = 210 cm³ and mass is 600 g. Their ratio is 20/7 g/cm³.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An object weighs 147 N where gravitational acceleration is 9.8 m/s². What are its mass and weight at a site where the acceleration is 1.6 m/s²?
questions.explanation: The mass is 147/9.8 = 15 kg everywhere. At the second site it weighs 15×1.6 = 24 N.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 10 kg box rests on a level floor. Its coefficient of static friction is 0.30 and g = 10 m/s². A horizontal pull of 26 N is applied. What friction force acts on it?
questions.explanation: Static friction adjusts to balance the 26 N pull because the required force is below the 30 N limit.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 4 kg object speeds up from 3 m/s to 7 m/s. What is the net work done on it?
questions.explanation: The work–energy theorem gives ΔK = ½ × 4 × (49−9) = 80 J.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A motor raises a 50 kg load through 6 m in 20 s at steady speed. With g = 10 m/s² and efficiency of 75%, what is the input power?
questions.explanation: Useful power is 50×10×6/20 = 150 W. Since that is 75% of input, the motor takes 200 W.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal lever raises a 240 N load vertically by 5 cm. The effort point moves 20 cm in the direction of the applied force. What effort force is required?
questions.explanation: Equal input and output work gives effort × 20 = 240 × 5 in N·cm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 600 W heater operates for 2 minutes. Seventy percent of its energy heats 0.4 kg of water of specific heat capacity 4,200 J/(kg·°C). What is the temperature rise?
questions.explanation: The water receives 0.7×600×120 = 50,400 J. Dividing by 0.4×4,200 gives a rise of 30°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 Ω resistor and an 8 Ω resistor are connected in parallel across 24 V. When the 12 Ω branch is disconnected, by what percentage does the supply current decrease?
questions.explanation: The two initial currents are 2 A and 3 A. The supply current drops from 5 A to 3 A, a 40% decrease.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 900 W heater runs 40 minutes daily for 14 days. How much electrical energy does it use?
questions.explanation: Convert to 0.9 kW and 2/3 hour daily. The product 0.9×2/3×14 is 8.4 kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 10 kg trolley starts from rest. Forces of 28 N east and 8 N west act on it for 4 s. What speed does it reach?
questions.explanation: The net force is 20 N east, so the acceleration is 2 m/s². In 4 s it gains 8 m/s of speed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sheet measures 18 cm by 25 cm with a thickness of 3.6 mm. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert 3.6 mm to 0.36 cm before multiplying 18×25×0.36.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A liquid has density 1.2 g/cm³. What is the mass of 1.5 L of the liquid?
questions.explanation: The volume is 1,500 cm³, giving mass of 1,800 g or 1.8 kg.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear thermometer shows 5 units in melting ice and 95 units in boiling water at standard pressure. What Celsius temperature corresponds to a reading of 59 units?
questions.explanation: The reading is 54 of the 90 scale units above zero Celsius. Thus the temperature is 100×54/90 = 60°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Three vertical rope segments equally support a 210 N load in an ideal pulley system. With ropes and pulleys ideal, how much rope must be pulled to lift the load by 0.8 m?
questions.explanation: All three supporting segments shorten by 0.8 m, so the free end moves through 3×0.8 m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 25 kg trolley moves at 10 m/s on a horizontal track. A constant 250 N force opposes the motion. How far does the trolley travel before stopping?
questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy is ½×25×100 = 1,250 J. The braking force uses that energy over 1,250/250 metres.

questions.question: Three counters A, B and C sold 70, 90 and 110 tickets in some order. A sold more than B, and C did not sell 70. What is the number sold by B?

questions.question: Four services A, B, C and D last 30, 40, 60 and 80 minutes, all different. A takes twice as long as B, C is longer than D, and D is not the shortest. Which service takes 60 minutes?

It has been accepted for delivery.
It is labelled and within the mass limit.

questions.question: P is true only if Q is true. R is true exactly when Q is false. If R is true, which truth values are forced for P and Q?

questions.subject: Logical Capability

questions.question: M is the sister of N. N is the father of P. Q is P’s son. How is M related to Q?

The west entrance has the lowest footfall at all times.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete the series 8, 13, 23, 38, 58, …

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: What comes next in 7, 21, 17, 51, 47, 141, …?
questions.explanation: The operations alternate between multiplying by three and subtracting four.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete 3, 24, 6, 20, 12, 16, 24, …
questions.explanation: The odd-position terms double. The even-position terms decrease by four, so the eighth term is 12.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete the series BD, EG, IK, NP, …
questions.explanation: Each pair has a two-letter gap in position. The first letters advance by 3, 4, 5, then 6 from N to T, giving TV.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The first, second and third letters of a word are shifted forward by 2, 4 and 1 places respectively, wrapping after Z. The result is then reversed. How is CAR coded?
questions.explanation: C advances to E, A to E and R to S. Reverse EES to get SEE.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a code, red signal reads ni ta, red lamp reads ni po, and green lamp reads su po. How is green signal written in the same adjective–noun order?
questions.explanation: Green is su and signal is ta, based on the repeated words.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Pentagon is to five diagonals as octagon is to how many diagonals?
questions.explanation: Each octagon vertex has five nonadjacent vertices. Counting each diagonal twice gives 8×5/2 = 20.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Which pair does not obey the rule that the second number is the product of the distinct prime factors of the first?
questions.explanation: The distinct prime factors of 48 are 2 and 3, whose product is 6. The other pairs follow the rule.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Nila is 17th from the front of a queue. Omar is 12th from the back and stands four places behind Nila. How many people are in the queue?
questions.explanation: Omar is 21st from the front. Add 21 and 12 and subtract one because Omar is counted twice.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: M is 8th from the left in a row of 27. N is 6th from the right. After M and N swap, what is M’s rank from the left?
questions.explanation: N’s original position from the left is 27−6+1 = 22. M moves there.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A person walks 8 m east, 6 m north, 2 m west and 1 m south. In which direction is the final point from the start?
questions.explanation: The net displacement is 6 m east and 5 m north, in the north-east quadrant.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: If letters in STATION are written in alphabetical order, which letter is third from the right?
questions.explanation: The ordering is A, I, N, O, S, T, T. Third from the right is S.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Five files P, Q, R, S, T are placed in a row. P is before Q, R is immediately after S, and T is first. Q is last. Which file must be fourth if P is second?
questions.explanation: T and Q occupy the ends and P is second. The consecutive pair S–R fills slots three and four.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A sits immediately to the left of B. Two people sit between B and E, with E to B’s right. C sits immediately to the right of B. In a row of five occupied entirely by A–E, who sits immediately left of E?
questions.explanation: The positions are forced to A, B, C, D, E.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Choose the pair following the same rule as 13:170, where the second number is one more than the square of the first.
questions.explanation: Sixteen squared is 256, and adding one gives 257.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Four files P, Q, R and S are placed in a line. P must precede Q, and R must precede S. How many orders are possible?
questions.explanation: Choose the two positions for P and Q in 4 choose 2 ways. The remaining positions are filled by R then S.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: K is taller than M but shorter than P. Q is shorter than P and taller than K. Of P, Q, K and M, who is second tallest?
questions.explanation: The clues give the strict order P, Q, K, M from tallest to shortest.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A mapping sends 12 to 6 and 23 to 14 by adding one to the sum of the squares of its digits. What does it send 34 to?
questions.explanation: For 34, the rule gives 3²+4²+1 = 26.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next number in 4, 12, 24, 72, 144, …
questions.explanation: The multipliers alternate between three and two. The next operation is ×3.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A code substitutes every letter with its alphabetic mirror, so A becomes Z and B becomes Y. What word is encoded as GIRK?
questions.explanation: The inverse mirror substitutions give G→T, I→R, R→I and K→P.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A small depot handles 60 consignments with mean processing time 12 minutes and a larger depot handles 90 with mean time 20 minutes. Nine consignments at the larger depot took 10 minutes each and are excluded. What is the mean processing time of the remaining 141 consignments to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: The adjusted total is 60×12+90×20−9×10 = 2,430 minutes, and 2,430/141 ≈ 17.23.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 12 hours. A leak can empty the full tank in 18 hours. At constant rates, how long will the pipe take to fill the remaining two-thirds of the tank with the leak open?
questions.explanation: The net rate is 1/12−1/18 = 1/36 tank per hour. Filling two-thirds takes (2/3)×36 hours.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two runners start together on a 360 m circular track and run in opposite directions at constant speeds of 5 m/s and 7 m/s. How long after starting do they first meet again?
questions.explanation: The two runners together cover one lap at a combined speed of 12 m/s. Divide 360 by 12.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two trains 180 m and 220 m long move towards each other at 54 and 90 km/h. How long do they take to pass each other completely, starting when the fronts meet?
questions.explanation: The closing speed is 144 km/h = 40 m/s. Both lengths, totalling 400 m, must pass.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A supplier sells two items for ₹960 each. On one it gains 20% and on the other it loses 20%. What is its overall result?
questions.explanation: The cost prices are ₹800 and ₹1,200, totalling ₹2,000. The ₹1,920 received is 4% lower.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An older sibling is 6 years older than a younger sibling. Four years ago the older sibling was twice the age of the younger one. What is the sum of their current ages?
questions.explanation: If the younger sibling is x, then x+2 = 2(x−4), so x = 10. Their current ages sum to 26.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A hall has 16 rows. The first has 12 seats, and each successive row has 7 more seats than the previous one. How many seats are in the hall?
questions.explanation: The last row has 12+15×7 = 117 seats. Multiply the average of the first and last rows by 16.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: What is the remainder when 2 to the ninth power multiplied by 3 to the fifth power is divided by 7?
questions.explanation: Since 2³ leaves remainder 1, so does 2⁹. The remainder of 3⁵ is 5 because 3²≡2 and 3⁴≡4 modulo 7.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that their sum is 9 or that both dice show the same number?
questions.explanation: Four ordered outcomes sum to 9 and six are doubles. The two events are disjoint, giving 10/36.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A bag holds 3 white and 5 black counters. Two counters are drawn independently with replacement. What is the probability of drawing at least one white counter?
questions.explanation: The probability of two black draws is (5/8)² = 25/64. Subtract it from one.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: At the same moment on level ground, a vertical 1.6 m post casts a 2.4 m shadow and a tower casts an 18 m shadow. What is the tower’s height?
questions.explanation: The height-to-shadow ratio is shared because the sun’s elevation is the same. Multiply 18 by 1.6/2.4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: In an 8 m square, a quarter circle of radius 4 m is drawn inside each corner. The quarter circles touch without overlapping. What area lies outside all four sectors?
questions.explanation: Four quarter circles make one complete radius-4 circle, of area 16π m². Subtract it from 64 m².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Water fills a pipe of radius 2 cm and moves at 25 m/min. At what rate is water delivered in litres per minute?
questions.explanation: The cross-section is 4π cm² and the speed is 2,500 cm/min. The resulting 10,000π cm³/min is 10π L/min.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A dataset is 4, 7, 9, 12, 13 and 15. If the largest value is changed to 45, by how much do the mean and median increase respectively?
questions.explanation: The total increases by 30 across six values. The middle two observations remain 9 and 12.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Which expression gives the SI unit of pressure in terms of kilograms, metres and seconds?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force divided by area. Dividing kg·m/s² by m² gives kg/(m·s²).

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: In an insulated vessel, 200 g of water at 70°C is mixed with 300 g of water at 20°C. Neglect the heat capacity of the vessel. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: Equal specific heats make the final temperature the mass-weighted average: (200×70+300×20)/500.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two blocks of equal mass receive the same amount of heat. Block X warms up by 18°C and block Y by 12°C, with no heat losses. What is the ratio of X’s specific heat capacity to Y’s?
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity is inversely proportional to the rise when added heat and mass are the same.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 4 Ω resistor and an 8 Ω resistor are in series across an ideal 24 V source. What power is dissipated in the 8 Ω resistor?
questions.explanation: The circuit current is 24/(4+8) = 2 A. The 8 Ω resistor dissipates I²R = 32 W.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 1.2 kW appliance operates for 45 minutes each day for 20 days. At ₹7.50 per kWh, what is its energy cost?
questions.explanation: The energy used is 1.2×0.75×20 = 18 kWh, costing 18×7.50.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 20 kg box slides along a level floor with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.25. With g = 10 m/s², how much work does friction do while the box moves 6 m?
questions.explanation: The friction force is 0.25×200 = 50 N. Its work is negative because it opposes the 6 m displacement.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2 kg cart moves at 4 m/s. A net force transfers another 20 J of energy into its kinetic energy. What is the new speed?
questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy is 16 J. The new kinetic energy is 36 J and equals v² for a 2 kg cart.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two identical loads are lifted the same vertical distance at constant speed. Motor A takes 24 s and motor B takes 18 s. What is the ratio of B’s useful power to A’s useful power?
questions.explanation: The work is the same, so the power ratio is the inverse time ratio 24:18.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A real machine lifts a 360 N load by 0.8 m while its input point moves 3 m. If its efficiency is 80%, what input force is needed along the motion?
questions.explanation: The useful work is 288 J. Input work is 288/0.8 = 360 J, requiring 120 N over 3 m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A rectangular metal block measures 10 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm. A 2 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm piece is cut out. The density is 7.5 g/cm³. What is the remaining mass?
questions.explanation: Volume falls from 200 to 160 cm³. Multiply by 7.5 g/cm³ to get 1,200 g.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A trolley covers 30 m in the first 5 s and 24 m in the next 3 s. What is its average speed over the full motion?
questions.explanation: The total distance is 54 m in 8 s, giving 54/8 = 6.75 m/s.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in parallel to an ideal source. What is the ratio of their dissipated powers, 6 Ω to 12 Ω?
questions.explanation: Their voltages are equal. Power is V²/R, so the 6 Ω resistor dissipates twice the power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2.0 m rail expands by 0.024 mm per degree Celsius over the temperature range considered. How long is it after a 50°C rise?
questions.explanation: The increase is 0.024×50 = 1.2 mm or 0.0012 m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 120 N load is 0.30 m to the left of a frictionless pivot. A second 60 N load is 0.20 m to the right. How far to the right must an additional 80 N load be placed to balance the lever?
questions.explanation: The left moment is 36 N·m and the existing right moment is 12 N·m. The remaining 24 N·m requires a 0.30 m arm for 80 N.

questions.question: Three counters A, B and C collect ₹9,600 in total. How much does A collect? I: A collects the same amount as B. II: C collects ₹2,400.
questions.explanation: Statement II gives A+B = ₹7,200, and I makes the split equal. Neither statement alone fixes A.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Is the combined punctuality rate of two stations above 80%? I: Each station’s rate exceeds 80%. II: They have equal departure counts.
questions.explanation: A weighted average of two rates above 80% is above 80%. Equal counts alone give no rate information.

questions.question: What is station X’s passenger count? I: X accounts for 40% of the three stations’ passengers. II: Station Y served 120 passengers.
questions.explanation: Y’s count alone does not fix the combined count because Z’s count is unknown. The 40% share cannot yet give a unique count.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Four counters A, B, C and D sold 40, 50, 60 and 70 tickets in some order. A sold 20 more than D, C sold more than B, and C did not sell 70. How many tickets did D sell?
questions.explanation: If A and D were 60 and 40, C would have to take 70 to exceed B. Therefore A and D are 70 and 50.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: The mean of four positive integer counts is 18. The largest is 26, the smallest is 10, and the other two differ by 4. What is the second largest count?
questions.explanation: The middle counts sum to 4×18−26−10 = 36. Two numbers with sum 36 and difference 4 are 16 and 20.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Every service is classified as delayed or on time. No delayed service was assigned platform 1. Some services assigned platform 1 were express. Which conclusion follows?
options: Some express services were on time.
No on-time service used a different platform.
questions.explanation: The platform 1 expresses cannot be delayed. Under the two-way classification they were on time.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which statement negates “Every parcel is checked and labelled”?
options: Every parcel is unchecked and unlabelled.
At least one parcel is checked and labelled.
No parcel is checked unless it is labelled.
At least one parcel is unchecked or unlabelled.
questions.explanation: One parcel failing either requirement is sufficient to make the universal statement false.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A lamp lights when exactly one of switches P and Q is closed. The lamp is dark while Q is open. What must be true?
options: P may be either open or closed.
questions.explanation: If P were closed with Q open, exactly one switch would be closed and the lamp would light.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: When between 2:00 and 3:00 do the clock hands first coincide?
questions.explanation: The hour hand starts 60° ahead. The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute. The time required is 60/5.5 = 120/11 minutes.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: In a non-leap year 1 February falls on Friday. What day is 1 May?
questions.explanation: The February, March and April lengths sum to 28+31+30 = 89 days. The remainder modulo 7 is five, shifting Friday to Wednesday.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Asha is the mother of siblings Bhanu and Chitra. Dev is Chitra’s son and Esha is Bhanu’s daughter. How are Dev and Esha related?
questions.explanation: Their parents are siblings, so they are first cousins.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A depot opts to add an online timetable to reduce calls asking when services leave. Which assumption is necessary for this reasoning?
options: Some callers can access the timetable instead of calling.
Every caller owns the same type of phone.
The depot will abolish telephone support.
Call volumes never change for other reasons.
questions.explanation: To replace some timetable calls, the online service needs to be usable by at least some of those callers.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A pilot programme claims that a new sign cut walking time to exits. Which fact most weakens the claim?
options: The sign used a new font and larger lettering.
The pilot recorded times for similar numbers of passengers before and after.
A temporary shortcut opened alongside the new sign and closed after the pilot.
Some passengers used an exit on the opposite side.
questions.explanation: A shortcut introduced at the same time could cut walking time without the sign having any effect.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Exactly two of four routes P, Q, R and S will operate. P can operate only with Q. R and Q cannot operate together. Which pair is possible?
questions.explanation: Only R and S avoid both a missing prerequisite for P and the Q–R conflict.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Exactly one of three boxes A, B and C contains a token. The labels are A: “The token is in C.” B: “The token is not in A.” C: “The token is not in C.” Exactly two labels are true. Which conclusion follows?
options: The token must be in A.
The token must be in B.
The token is in B or C.
The token must be in C.
questions.explanation: The labels on A and C are complements, so precisely one is true. B’s label must also be true, excluding box A.

Fixed hours make it easier to predict when the library opens.
The same policy would increase visits in every village.
questions.explanation: The trial examined one library. Its results do not establish that every village would respond the same way.
questions.passage: A rural library used to announce its evening opening times week by week. It began a trial with fixed evenings so readers could plan their visits. Volunteers still helped first-time visitors use the catalogue and borrowing desk. The team counted both first-time and repeat visits, and compared evenings with and without late buses to see whether transport might influence turnout. It planned to review those records before deciding whether to extend the trial.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete 5, 12, 23, 38, 57, …
questions.explanation: The differences are 7, 11, 15 and 19. The next difference is 23.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete 3, 15, 6, 13, 12, 11, …
questions.explanation: The next term is in an odd position, where the sequence doubles: 3, 6, 12, 24.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: What comes next in 2, 5, 12, 27, 58, …?
questions.explanation: Double each term and add successive integers starting at 1. The next value is 2×58+5.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: What pair follows CL, FK, IJ, LI, …?
questions.explanation: First letters advance by three positions. Second letters move one position back. L→O and I→H give OH.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Shift letters at odd positions forward one step and letters at even positions backward one step. How is TRAIN coded?
questions.explanation: T→U, R→Q, A→B, I→H and N→O.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A word is first reversed and then each letter is advanced two places, wrapping over Z. If the output is GVCT, what was the input?
questions.explanation: Shifting back gives ETAR. Reversing gives RATE.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a code that preserves word order, blue board reads ke ru, blue lamp reads ke fu, and bright lamp reads so fu. What is bright board?
questions.explanation: Bright corresponds to so and board corresponds to ru.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Which pair follows the same rule as 14:196 and 17:289?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first. Nineteen squared is 361.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Which number is the exception to the rule followed by 27, 64, 125 and 200?
questions.explanation: 27, 64 and 125 are the cubes of 3, 4 and 5. Two hundred is not a perfect cube.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: An hour is to 3,600 seconds as 2.5 minutes is to how many seconds?
questions.explanation: Multiplying minutes by 60 gives 2.5×60 = 150 seconds.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: L is 9th from the front of a 28-person queue. M stands six places behind L. What is M’s position from the back?
questions.explanation: M is 15th from the front. Counting from the back gives 28−15+1 = 14.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Ami is 10th from the left and 14th from the right in a row. Three people join at the left end and two at the right end. What is Ami’s new position from the right?
questions.explanation: Only the two additions at the right end affect Ami’s rank from the right.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Five seats from left to right are filled by R, S, T, U and V. T is directly between S and U, S is left of U, R is at the far right, and V is left of S. Which person is third?
questions.explanation: The constraints force V, S, T, U, R. T occupies the middle seat.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Six tasks P, Q, R, S, T and U are done one at a time. P is immediately before Q, R is immediately after T, S is first, and U is last. If R comes before Q, which task is fourth?
questions.explanation: The middle blocks occur in the order T–R then P–Q. The complete order is S, T, R, P, Q, U.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: From a starting point, Sana walks 12 m south and 5 m west. What straight-line distance separates Sana from that starting point?
questions.explanation: The legs are perpendicular so the distance is √(12²+5²) = 13 m.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: G scored more than H. H scored more than J. K scored less than G but more than H. L scored more than G. Who placed third from the top among the five?
questions.explanation: Descending order is L, G, K, H, J.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Four tasks K, L, M and N can be done in any order subject to K and L being consecutive in either order. How many schedules satisfy this condition?
questions.explanation: Treat K and L as a single block to get 3! arrangements. The block has two orientations, yielding 12.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Write PLATFORM in alphabetical order, retaining every letter. Which letter is fifth from the left?
questions.explanation: The sorted letters are A, F, L, M, O, P, R, T, so the fifth letter is O.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A two-digit code replaces a number by twice its units digit plus three times its tens digit. What number does 57 produce?

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Beginning again at A after Z, find the next letter in W, Z, D, I, …
questions.explanation: The advances are +3, +4 and +5 with wraparound. Add six to I to obtain O.
